Of course. This is an excellent and realistic scenario. Here is a specific, actionable approach tailored to the nonprofit's constraints. ### Executive Summary The recommended approach is a **simple, offline-first system** using rugged, affordable tablets and a free, open-source data collection platform called **KoboToolbox**. This strategy prioritizes ease of use for staff with low digital literacy, works reliably without internet or stable electricity in the field, and is financially sustainable after the initial 18-month funding period ends. The total estimated cost is **PHP 395,500**, leaving a small contingency from the PHP 400,000 budget. --- ### 1. The Recommended Approach: "Simple, Offline-First, and Sustainable" The core philosophy is to equip field staff with tools that work 100% offline and only require a connection when they return to the office to upload data. This avoids frustration and ensures data is captured regardless of field conditions. **How it works:** 1. **Form Creation:** A manager or designated "Data Champion" uses a web browser at the main office to create simple digital forms (e.g., Patient Registration, Home Visit Checklist, Health Survey). These forms look just like the paper versions staff are used to. 2. **Offline Data Collection:** Field staff use a simple app on their tablets to fill out these forms. They can enter data, take photos, and capture GPS locations, all without an internet connection. The app saves all entries securely on the tablet. 3. **Data Syncing:** Once a week (or whenever they are back at the office), staff connect their tablet to the office Wi-Fi. With one tap in the app, all the collected data is automatically uploaded to a central, secure server. 4. **Analysis & Reporting:** The manager can then log in to the central server to view the aggregated data, see it on a map, generate simple charts, and export it to Excel for reporting to donors and the Department of Health. ### 2. Specific Tools and Platforms | Component | Recommended Tool | Why it's the right choice | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Data Collection Software** | **KoboToolbox** | **Free & Open Source:** Developed by the Harvard Humanitarian Initiative, it's free for humanitarian and nonprofit organizations. No subscription fees, ever.
**Offline-First:** The `KoboCollect` Android app is designed specifically for offline data collection in challenging environments.
**Simple Interface:** The app is incredibly easy for field staff to use. It's just a series of questions they tap through.
**Powerful Forms:** You can build forms with skip logic (e.g., if 'Patient is pregnant', show pregnancy-related questions), photo capture, GPS points, and multiple languages (English/Tagalog). | | **Field Hardware (for ~25 field staff)** | **Android Tablets (e.g., Samsung Galaxy Tab A7 Lite or a local brand like Cherry Mobile Aqua Tab)** | **Cost-Effective:** These tablets offer the best balance of screen size, battery life, and price. A larger screen is easier to use than a small phone for forms.
**Good Battery Life:** 8-10 hours of use, enough for a full day in the field.
**Android OS:** Required to run the `KoboCollect` app. | | **Field Power** | **High-Capacity Power Banks (e.g., Anker or Romoss 20,000mAh)** | **Essential for Intermittent Electricity:** A 20,000mAh power bank can recharge a tablet 2-3 times, ensuring staff can work for several days without access to a wall outlet. | | **Office Hardware** | **Mid-Range Laptop (e.g., Lenovo IdeaPad, Acer Aspire)** | **Central Hub:** One reliable laptop is needed at the main office for the program manager or "Data Champion" to create forms, manage the KoboToolbox account, and analyze incoming data. | | **Office Connectivity** | **Basic Business Fiber Internet Plan (e.g., from PLDT or Converge)** | **The Sync Point:** A single, reliable internet connection is only needed at the main office for uploading data from the tablets and managing the system. | --- ### 3. What Happens When Donor Funding Ends in 18 Months? This plan is explicitly designed for long-term sustainability with minimal to zero recurring costs. * **No Software Fees:** **KoboToolbox is free.** The organization will not face any software subscription costs after the 18 months. This is the single most important factor for financial sustainability. * **Minimal Running Costs:** The only recurring operational cost is the **office internet bill (approx. PHP 2,000/month)**. This is a standard utility that the organization would likely need anyway and can be built into its core operational budget. * **Internal Capacity:** The 18-month period will be used to train one or two staff members to become the internal **"Data Champions."** They will be the experts who can create new forms, train new staff, and troubleshoot minor issues. The initial grant pays for their expert training, making this knowledge a permanent asset of the organization. * **Hardware Lifecycle:** The tablets and power banks have a realistic lifespan of 3-4 years if cared for properly (hence the budget for rugged cases). The organization can plan ahead and include a small hardware replacement fund in future grant proposals or operational budgets, asking for PHP 50,000 every 3 years instead of a massive one-time digitisation grant. By the end of the 18 months, the nonprofit will not be dependent on the donor. It will fully own the hardware and possess the internal skills to manage a robust, free, and effective digital data system perfectly suited to its operating environment.
